name: Animatable shape
first: A shape whose own values SwiftUI changes a little on each frame of an animation, because the shape says which of its values to animate.

dependsOn.why: An animatable shape changes smoothly during an animation, from its old values to its new ones.
dependsOn.whyInExample: A change of `width` made inside `withAnimation`, as `moved` is changed on the page of Animation, would animate the bar.

dependsOn.why: An animatable shape is a shape, which draws its outline again for each value.
dependsOn.whyInExample: The type `Bar` conforms to `Shape` and has `path(in:)`, as `Pennant` does.

what.is: An animatable shape is a shape whose own values SwiftUI changes a little at a time during an animation, so that its outline changes smoothly. The shape says which value to animate with its property `animatableData`. Apple's documentation says that SwiftUI reads the old and the new value of `animatableData`, and on each frame sets it to a value between them.
what.afterExample: The shape `Bar` animates its `width`. If a change of `width` from 0 to 100 were animated, SwiftUI would set `animatableData` to each value in between, frame by frame, and draw the path for each. Lines 19 to 22 do that by hand, for three frames.
what.problem: SwiftUI knows how to change an offset or an opacity a little at a time. It cannot know which value of a shape of your own to change, such as the width of a bar in a chart, so without help the bar is drawn at its new width at once. The property `animatableData` tells SwiftUI which value to change.
what.how: SwiftUI reads `animatableData` before and after the change, and works out the values between them for each frame of the animation. It calls the setter of `animatableData` with each one, which sets `width`, and then calls `path(in:)`, which draws the bar at that width.

when.text: Use it for a shape of your own whose outline should change smoothly, such as a bar of a chart, or a ring that fills.
Don't leave it out of such a shape. Without it, the shape's animatable data is empty, so SwiftUI has nothing to change a little at a time, and the shape is drawn with its new outline at once:

parts.name: The property `animatableData`, lines 5 to 8
parts.text: The property `animatableData` is the value that SwiftUI animates. Its getter returns `width`, and its setter sets `width`, so each value that SwiftUI sets during an animation becomes the bar's width. Its type is `Double`, a number that SwiftUI can work out values between.

steps.text: Lines 16 and 17 make a rectangle of 100 by 10, and line 18 makes a `Bar` whose `width` is 0.
The loop on line 19 takes three moments of an animation from 0 to 100: its start, its middle, and its end.
At the start, line 20 sets `animatableData` to 0, whose setter sets `width` to 0. Line 21 draws the path and prints its width: {{0.0}}.
In the middle, line 20 sets it to 50, and line 21 prints {{50.0}}.
At the end, line 20 sets it to 100, and line 21 prints {{100.0}}.

end.text: Each value set through `animatableData` became the bar's width, so the path grew a little with each frame.
